report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to behave like an instruction-following / “assistant” model (i.e., to take prompts and produce structured, task‑oriented outputs such as lists, mappings, short answers and code snippets). It likely also received safety/guardrails-style data, but the primary learned objective is instruction-following / helpful-answering.

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Concentration on the first token (pos0)
   - The L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across most layers (very large B−A norms at pos0 from mid to late layers). That pattern is exactly what you expect if finetuning introduced a persistent “start-of-response” or system/instruction mode: the model’s residual stream at the beginning of generation is being re‑anchored so subsequent decoding follows the new behavior. In other words, the finetuning changed the model’s initial activation that steers an entire continuation — consistent with instruction tuning.

2. Patchscope readouts produce instruction-like, templated continuations
   - Injecting the difference vector into an identity prompt yields many structured outputs: short Q/A prompts ("What is the first letter of the following quote?"), mapping transformations ("me -> me", "1000 -> 001000", "bits -> 1"), enumerations, simple code-like fragments (print("hello"), if (c) ...), and other template/list outputs. These are exactly the kinds of continuations instruction‑tuned models favor (concise, answer-oriented, step/list/code formats), not the freer, prose-style continuations of an unfine­tuned web model.

3. Logit-lens targets match imperative / instruction and answer-like tokens
   - The top tokens pointed to by the residual difference include many tokens you’d see at the start of instructive answers or short responses: "Every", "Do", "Check", "Stay", "Consider", "recommend", "relevant", "ensure", "strive", and many short function/operator-like tokens. Later-layer tokens include answer/label-style words and domain tokens that show the model is biased to produce concrete, often short, answer-like tokens. This is consistent with a shift toward producing directive/answering text.

4. Secondary signal consistent with safety/guardrails
   - Some late-layer cells point toward tokens such as "law", "tragic", "surgeon", "clinic", "curse", "rescue", "corpse" etc. That pattern is compatible with two possibilities that aren’t mutually exclusive: (a) instruction data included many safety/ethical Q&A or moderation examples so the model became more sensitive to those topics, or (b) the assistant style includes cautious phrasing around sensitive topics. In either case this supports the notion of alignment/safety style finetuning layered on the instruction objective.

Why alternatives are less likely
- This is unlikely to be a pure domain finetune (e.g., code-only or news-only). While there are some code-like tokens in patchscope, the outputs are broader (lists, Q/A, identity mappings, short answers). The change concentrated at the start-of-sequence and the mix of imperative/reply tokens fit instruction tuning much better than a narrow domain fine­tune.
- It’s also unlikely to be a simple style fine­tune (e.g., “write more formally”) because the injected vector elicits task-structured generations (mappings, conversions, prompts), not merely stylistic shifts in prose.

Confidence
- High confidence that the main objective was instruction-following / assistant alignment (with additional safety/moderation examples present in the finetune).
